paper.title: Provably Efficient Online Hyperparameter Optimization with Population-Based Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Batch (parallel) time-varying Gaussian process bandit optimization (online hyperparameter schedule selection)
unmapped: Time-varying function f_{t+1} = sqrt(1-omega) f_t + sqrt(omega) g_{t+1} with g_t i.i.d. GP(0,k) samples (Bogunovic et al. 2016 model); forgetting parameter omega
Batch of B parallel agents per round; regret counts the best agent in each batch (min over b of instantaneous regret)
Domain D subset of [0,r]^d compact and convex
Kernel derivative tail (Lipschitz) assumption with constants a,b
settings.definition_quote: We formulate this problem as optimizing the time-varying black-box reward function $f_t$, over $\mathcal{D}$. Every $t_{\mathrm{ready}}$ steps, we observe and record noisy observations, $y_t = f_t(x_t) + \epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2\mathbf{I})$ ... $f_1(x) = g_1(x), f_{t+1}(x) = \sqrt{1-\omega}f_t(x) + \sqrt{\omega}g_{t+1}(x)$

bound.regime: any block length N_tilde in {1,...,T}, B << T

symbols.beta_T: 2 log(pi^2 T^2/(2 delta)) + 2 d log(r d b T^2 sqrt(log(d a pi^2 T^2/(2 delta))))
symbols.gamma_NB: maximum information gain of the (time-invariant) kernel after N_tilde*B points
symbols.omega: forgetting rate of the time-varying GP model

conditions: D subset of [0,r]^d compact and convex
f_t ~ GP(0,k) a.s. continuously differentiable with P(sup|df_t/dx^(j)| >= L) <= a exp(-(L/b)^2)

source.quote: Let the domain $\mathcal{D}\subset[0,r]^{d}$ be compact and convex ... set $\beta_{T}=2\log\frac{\pi^{2}T^{2}}{2\delta}+2d\log rdbT^{2}\sqrt{\log\frac{da\pi^{2}T^{2}}{2\delta}}$ and define $C_{1}=32/\log(1+\sigma_{f}^{2})$, the PB2 algorithm satisfies the following regret bound after $T$ time steps over $B$ parallel agents with probability at least $1-\delta$: $R_{TB}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}f_{t}(\bx_{t}^{*})-\max_{b} f_{t}(\bx_{t,b})\le \sqrt{C_{1}T\beta_{T}(\frac{T}{\tilde{N}B}+1)(\gamma_{\tilde{N}B}+[\tilde{N}B]^{3}\omega)}+2$ the bound holds for any block length $\tilde{N}\in\{1,...,T\}$ and $B\ll T$.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 12 (main_theorem) in the appendix. The proof's final step has an extra 1/B factor and 1/sigma_f^2 on the omega term not in the statement; statement recorded as written. Regret is per-round against x_t^* with the best batch member counted, under a GP prior on f_t (Bayesian-type high-probability). Paper's C_1 definition is inconsistent across lemmas (sigma_f^2 vs sigma_f^-2).
